A ring of toppled basalt monoliths arranged in a broken circle on the foreground plain, each fallen stone the length of a ship-hull, the surviving uprights twice the height of a watchtower, the enclosed floor as bare and wide as a cathedral nave.

A titan-torso buried to the chest in the deep-distance plain, both stone arms raised and frozen mid-gesture, the broad shoulders forming a saddle-ridge between the arms, the posture of supplication readable as terrain from the foreground.

A concentric henge of runic megaliths occupying the foreground hilltop in five nested rings, each ring separated by a ditch wide enough to float a river-barge, the outermost stones taller than a ship-mast and wider than a gatehouse.

A battlefield of standing spears covering the full midground plain, ten thousand shafts driven into frozen ground at uniform angles, pennants long rotted, the forest of pale poles reading as dense bristling texture from the foreground ridge.

A glowing portal-arch of assembled runic blocks spanning the deep-distance valley mouth, the keystone inscribed with a sigil the size of a barn-face, the arch framing a faintly distorted view of the landscape beyond its interior.

A petrified tidal-bore at the deep-distance coast, a wall of stone-frozen sea the height of a cathedral tower advancing permanently inland, gulls roosting in the stone-foam at its crest-line as though it were a cliff.

A dragon-ribcage exposed on the midground hillside by landslide, ribs arching from a central spine-ridge still buried in the slope, each bone the diameter of a siege-tower, the cavities between them open and deep enough to shelter a granary.

A titan-hand of pale granite emerging vertically from the midground hillside, all five fingers pressed together and pointing skyward, the distance from wrist to fingertip equal to the height of a cathedral tower, the wrist-joint still buried in the slope.

A sacred oracle-throne of dark basalt suspended over the midground chasm on a natural stone pedestal, the backrest a sheer vertical face taller than a cathedral spire, the armrests overhanging a sheer drop on either side.

A fallen giant-shoulder and outstretched arm lying across the midground hillside, the deltoid rendered in cracked grey stone forming a hill in its own right, the open palm at deep distance cupping a standing pool of still rainwater.

A rusted battle-standard of stone-petrified fabric draped over the midground ridgeline, its charging-beast motif pressed flat against the hillcrest, the banner wider than a city block and heavy enough to have split the ridge stone beneath it.

A titan-skull face-down in the midground swamp, the occipital crest forming a curved ridge above the waterline, the scale declared by willow trees rooted inside the eye-socket cavities with room for their full crowns to spread.

A crystal-spire eruption covering the foreground basin floor, translucent amber columns rising from pale soil, the tallest matching the surrounding cliffs, the field refracting dawn light into a continuous carpet of moving color across the valley walls.

A petrified dragon-claw erupting from the foreground earth at a raking angle, the three talons spread and each one curving to a point at the height of a cathedral tower, the knuckle-ridge half-buried in fractured stone.

A judgment-stone seat carved from a lone summit at deep distance, the throne-back one vertical cliff-face, the seat a broad horizontal shelf, the armrests two natural buttresses flanking a sheer drop that descends to the midground valley floor.

A leyline confluence pool glowing gold at the midground valley junction, four luminous channels converging on it from the cardinal hills, each channel wide as a river and etched visibly into the stone faces of the valley sides.

A dragon-wing arch spanning the deep-distance canyon mouth, the membrane long gone but the hollow bone framework intact, each primary spar the length of an aqueduct arch and as thick as a watchtower wall, the span dwarfing the canyon below.

A fallen-king throne half-consumed by deep-distance forest, its stone armrests emerging from the canopy like ruined cliffs, the seat basin wide enough to hold a standing body of water, the scale readable only by the full canopy pressed against its sides.

A levitating ring of boulders encircling the midground sky in a perfect horizontal band, each stone the size of a mill-tower, the ring casting a moving crescent shadow on the landscape below as it turns with the passage of the sun.

A titan-arm reaching from the midground lake at an upward angle, the stone elbow breaking the surface and the open hand aimed at the sky, the distance from elbow to fingertip wider than the lake is narrow at that point.

A frozen river-wave of solid ice at the midground valley base, the entire river halted mid-torrent, the crest-wall taller than a cathedral facade, transparent enough to show the dark shapes of water and stone locked motionless within.

A fossilized dragon-spine arching across the foreground valley in a lateral curve, each vertebral segment the size of a granary building forming a pale continuous causeway, the ridge casting a shadow wider than a cathedral nave across the meadow below.

A titan-shoulder and collarbone jutting from the midground hillside at a steep angle, the exposed clavicle forming a natural ridgeline wider than a cathedral nave from end to end, a stand of full-grown pines rooted along its upper surface.

A broken war-axe driven blade-first into the far cliff face at deep distance, the crescent blade wedged at height with its cutting edge as long as a harbor-wall section, the old-growth forest gathered at the cliff-base entirely dwarfed below it.

A hollow world-tree of silver bark standing at the horizon, its outer diameter wider than a town square, light bleeding through the latticed bark in pale vertical columns, the internal galleries visible as dark arched voids stacked from root to crown.

A levitating flat-topped granite mass the size of a castle courtyard suspended in the upper midground sky, its raw jagged underside trailing four unbroken waterfalls to the valley floor, the permanent shadow beneath it darker than the surrounding cloud.

A cursed-blade graveyard stretching across the entire deep-distance plain, ten thousand sword hilts jutting from ash-pale earth at uniform depth, the rusted bristle of the field reading as dense iron texture from the foreground ridge.

A concentric henge of runic megaliths crowning the foreground hilltop in four nested rings, each ring separated by a ditch wide enough to float a river-barge, the outermost stones taller than a ship-mast and wider than a gatehouse.

A mountain-wide portrait carved into the deep-distance cliff face, the single closed eye spanning a full third of the escarpment height, carved lashes as thick as aqueduct arches, the nose left as an uncut natural promontory jutting from the rock.

A leyline confluence pool glowing deep amber at the midground valley junction, four luminous channels converging on it from the surrounding hills, each channel wide as a river and etched visibly into the stone faces of the valley sides.

A half-collapsed citadel clinging to the far ridge at deep distance, one round tower still upright as a thin vertical stroke against pale sky, the curtain wall tumbled down the slope as a river of cut blocks each the size of a cottage.

A titan-kneeling torso frozen mid-bow in the deep-distance plain, the broad back forming a flat plateau above the treeline, the bowed head pressed against the earth as a stone hill, the posture of submission readable as terrain from the foreground.
